comments.text: slices.Reverse(rows) doesn't fix the stale-record problem, it relies on an ordering that isn't guaranteed. The batch query has no ORDER BY, so row order is whatever SQLite returns, and the 'a record can only reference records that already exist' premise is false: relations can be updated after creation (an older record can be edited to reference a newer one), ids can be custom, and multi-level graphs can have several branches. E.g. create a, c->[a], b->[a], then update c->[a,b]: reversed order processes b first, b's cascade deletes c, and the stale preloaded c is then saved/deleted again with outdated data. The robust fix is to load only ids per batch and re-fetch each record right before processing it (skipping ones that no longer exist).
Reversal also interacts with batching: when there are more referencing rows than batchSize, ordering only applies within one batch, so cross-batch dependencies are still processed with stale data.
No regression test is included for the nested self-referenced cascade scenario described in the PR; please add one, including a case where an older record references a newer one.
